Laboratory Assessment
Carbohydrate metabolism
Fasting blood glucose levels are usually in the normal range, but the glucose tolerance curve has been reported to be ﬂatter and often
with a double humped curve, suggestive of delayed absorption. There is an increased incidence of both Type 1 (insulin dependent)
and Type 2 diabetes in Down's syndrome. Studies have shown increased insulin resistance in obese and overweight females and
adults with Down's syndrome but further research is required.

Down's syndrome: Nutritional aspects


Protein Metabolism
Disturbances in protein metabolism are common in Down's syndrome. An increased level of immunoglobulin A and immunoglob-
ulin G antibodies to food antigens has been reported, and several studies have reported an increased prevalence of celiac disease.
Abnormal levels of fasting plasma and urinary amino acids have been reported.
